meta.description: Registry of minimal local theorems, propositions, and conjectures.

theorems.name: Projection Idempotence Under Stable Admissibility
theorems.statement: Pi_A(Pi_A(x)) ~ Pi_A(x) under stable admissibility conditions SA-001 through SA-005.
assumptions: SA-003: Fixed point property for y in A

theorems.name: Transport Identity on Null Path
theorems.statement: NavT_identity(x) ~ x under identity transport conditions NI-001 through NI-005.

theorems.name: Continuation Requires Non-Empty Admissible Image
theorems.statement: existence(continuation_event) => image(Pi_A ∘ delta_selection(candidate_set)) != empty under conditions NEI-001 through NEI-005.
assumptions: NEI-003: Pi_A maps at least one candidate into window
NEI-004: delta has at least one admissible candidate after constraints
NEI-005: Residue/orientation do not eliminate all candidates

theorems.name: aRT Membership and Closure Preservation Lemma
theorems.statement: If an aRT satisfies its declared membership, distinction-preservation, admissible-ordering, and closure-support conditions, then an admissible update to one or more member RTs preserves aRT status provided those conditions remain satisfied after the update.

theorems.name: O_calculus Partial Composition Lemma
theorems.statement: Orientation transformations compose lawfully iff they preserve typed admissible continuation and closure class.

theorems.name: otimes Non-Identity Composition Lemma
theorems.statement: If X and Z are typed lawful process operands and X otimes_Y Z is defined under context Y, then the composition creates a lawful typed coupling without implying X = Z, X = X otimes_Y Z, or Z = X otimes_Y Z, unless a separate identity-preserving rule is explicitly declared.

theorems.name: iff_s Projection Identity Firewall
theorems.statement: Statistical projection iff_s marks a representation layer and does not establish process identity.

theorems.name: Constraint Geometry Triadic Knot-Closure
theorems.statement: Within these models, Constraint Geometry is represented as the triadic geometric closure of RT, QM_app, and GR_app, restating the Core co-generative relation as a geometric knot-closure.

theorems.name: Projection Signature Hardening Rules
theorems.statement: Within these models, a Projection Signature (Sig_app) is represented as a recognizable pattern of constraints, outputs, and preserved relations showing that a process expression has lawfully projected into an application-facing domain.

theorems.name: Typed Zero-Condition Recoupling Principle
theorems.statement: Within these models, a locally collapsed same-direction expression may participate in higher-order RT only if its zero-condition remains typed and is compared against an oppositely typed zero-condition.

theorems.name: RT Nesting, Condition Primacy, and Family Constitution Principle
theorems.statement: Within these models, X is RT iff X constructively traces its dependency lineage to RT_core without breaking core constraints; distinction participants are process conditions, not states; and the minimum coupled nesting form is mutually constituted with the <*>_x family space.

theorems.name: RT Mechanics as Recursive Relational Completion
theorems.statement: Within these models, RT mechanics is provisionally defined by the reduction D(*|r) -> D(x|r) iff the field F' containing D(x|r) satisfies PRIN_001 closure traceable to RT_core, with x-admissibility and RT constitution mutually co-produced through residue-conditioned closure.
theorems.formula: D(*|r) -> D(x|r) iff F' containing D(x|r) satisfies PRIN_001 closure

theorems.name: Conditioning as Primitive Relational Process
theorems.statement: Within these models, conditioning is provisionally treated as the primitive relational process by which one distinction supplies admissibility context for another, with arithmetic operations interpreted only as derived projections of lawful conditioning order.

theorems.name: Primitive Conditioning Principle
theorems.statement: Within this provisional ontology reduction, the conditioned distinction <a>_b is treated as the smallest admissible RT-mechanics object, while D(a) is retained only as a context-suppressed abstraction.

theorems.name: Vertical Bar Operator Admissibility Principle
theorems.statement: Within these models, the vertical bar operator | is the primitive admissible participation separator, which is order-sensitive, requires type-checked operands, and gates co-participation as D(A|B) > epsilon_a.

theorems.name: Grouped Bar Closure Principle
theorems.statement: Within these models, grouped bar expressions require explicit graph co-participation closure Adm_|^G preserving consistent orientation, default to non-associative and non-permutable, and require mandatory middle term role typing in triadic structures.
theorems.formula: Adm_|^G(A_1,...,A_n; G) := [∀A_i Typed_a(A_i)] ∧ [∀e_ij ∈ E(G), Adm_|(A_i,A_j)] ∧ Preserve_O(G) ∧ Eval_D^G(G) ∧ D_G(G) > epsilon_a

theorems.name: Admissible Organization Axioms
theorems.statement: Within these models, the organization of co-participation graphs G under Org_a is governed by three axioms: Inventory Preservation (traceable distinction), Admissibility Conservation (no updates below epsilon_a), and Topological Consistency (orientation preservation).
theorems.formula: Adm_Org(G) := Adm_|^G(G) ∧ ∃o∈O(G) Adm_O(G,o) ∧ D_G(G)>epsilon_a ∧ InvPres_D(G) ∧ AdmCons_a(G) ∧ TopCons_O(G)

theorems.name: Core Calculus Syntax and Semantic Closure
theorems.statement: The core calculus of the Mono-Process Framework forms a syntactically and semantically closed language L_COD. All well-formed formulas map to distinct types, operators compose algebraically, natural deduction is sound, and satisfiability holds over graph-theoretic models.
theorems.formula: Closed_L_COD(L) := Syntax_Closed(L116) ∧ Semantic_Closed(L117) ∧ Closed_Algebra(L118) ∧ Sound_Deduction(L119) ∧ Satisfiable_Model(L120)

theorems.name: Ontological Distinction Emergence
theorems.statement: The operational existence of distinction emerges co-dependently from a primitive relational condition (*|*) via a domain-specific symmetric relational biconditional, resolving into an Affect-Effect gradient without reifying background coordinate space.

theorems.name: Relational Transition Core Equivalence
theorems.statement: A precursor distinction stabilizes into a Relational Transition if and only if it exceeds the context floor and forms a triadic closure cycle. The stabilized relational form is process-equivalent to the canonical core expression under local projection.

theorems.name: Asymmetry-to-Orientation Selection Operator
theorems.statement: Relational asymmetry breaks directional symmetry, permitting the selection operator O* to uniquely resolve to an oriented local reference frame -(i) that minimizes relational friction, regulated and bounded by the context floor.
theorems.formula: O*(Omega_a)_c := -(i) iff Omega_a != 1 ∧ Friction(-(i)) = min mu_rel(-(i') * Omega_a)

theorems.name: Sign Semantics and Generative Pathways
theorems.statement: Sign polarities (+, -) emerge dynamically to represent accumulation and exclusion dynamics along directed process pathways, preserving algebraic product rules through composition of crossing layer modifications.
theorems.formula: Sign(Delta P)_c := { + if Delta Crossings > 0, - if Delta Crossings < 0, 0 if Delta Crossings = 0 }

theorems.name: Evaluation Architecture and Governance Homomorphism
theorems.statement: Platform metadata governance represents a formal category-theoretic homomorphic projection of the underlying graph-theoretic relational admissibility transitions, preserving identities, composition, and collapse boundary mapping.

theorems.name: Functorial Braid Projection and Confinement
theorems.statement: Relational co-participation graph updates map functorially via F_proj to topological braids, where closed loops map to topological braid closures (knots/links) representing stable, self-reinforcing confinement regimes.

theorems.name: Polarity Closure and Nested Semantics
theorems.statement: The constraint realization loop (primary axiom) is recursively isomorphic to the generative tension between exclusion (-1) and accumulation (+1) pathways.
